title: Hangzhou, Again
body: Back in Hangzhou, the city where I first saw you. We wandered with no plan and ate with no restraint, letting the July heat do whatever it wanted. Two months ago I met your face for the first time here; today you fit into my afternoons as though you have always been in them.
quote: A city becomes different the second time you walk it with the same person.

title: Jinan
body: Took you to Jinan, my home ground. I showed you the springs the city is named for, and the streets that taught me to become who I am. You looked at all of it as if it were brand new, and through your eyes my own hometown became new to me too. I think that is the real gift of travelling with you — you give me back the places I stopped noticing.
quote: Home is not where you are from. It is where you stop being homesick.

title: Shanghai
body: Shanghai at night is a city trying very hard, and we loved it anyway. Bund lights spilled across the water, your hand in mine, a crowd that did not matter at all. You said the skyline looked like a promise someone had finally kept. I thought the exact same thing, only I was looking at you instead of the buildings.
quote: The best view in Shanghai was not across the river. It was right next to me.

title: Back to Hangzhou
body: We left Dali behind and flew home to Hangzhou, where this whole story had started only four days earlier. The flight was perfectly ordinary; the fact that we were on it together was not. I think a place becomes home the moment you return to it with someone waiting inside your phone, your plans, and your life.
quote: Coming home used to be the end of a trip. Now it is just another place I get to be with you.

title: Dali, and Us
body: This is the day, Zhaojin. Dali, Erhai Lake, the wind that would not sit still — and you, saying yes. We had been circling each other for two months, and here, far from everything familiar, we stopped circling and simply arrived. I had not planned what to say. I did not need to; you already knew, and so did I. In a town between mountains and water, we made us real.
quote: Some beginnings are quiet. This one was a whole landscape saying yes along with you.

title: First Sight, Hangzhou
body: The first time I actually saw you, in Hangzhou. We had known each other for two months through screens and words, and I had memorized your voice before I ever knew your face. We ate something delicious — I honestly cannot remember what, because I was too busy noticing how you laughed at your own jokes a beat before the punchline. After that meal, every meal without you felt like a small disappointment.
quote: I knew your mind for two months. It took one dinner in Hangzhou to know the rest of you.

title: In Words
body: Somewhere in April, with no date worth circling on a calendar, we said it out loud — that we were together. Not in person yet, not with any witnesses, just two voices deciding across a distance. It felt less like a decision and more like admitting something that had been true for weeks. We were not officially anything yet. We were already everything.
quote: The loudest promises are sometimes whispered through a phone at midnight.

title: How It Started
body: March. The beginning, though I did not know it then. We started talking — I forget about what, exactly, first — and I remember thinking your mind moved in a way I wanted to keep up with. I did not fall in love this month. I only started paying attention, which, I have since learned, is the very same thing happening slowly.
quote: I did not fall in love in March. I just started leaning in its direction.
